turns.text: How do you think cities will change in the next fifty years?
I suspect the most significant changes won't be the ones people currently predict. Everyone focuses on flying cars and so on, when the real shifts tend to be quieter
What sort of quiet shifts?
Demographic ones, mainly. A lot of cities are ageing rapidly, and an older population needs a fundamentally different kind of infrastructure
In what respect?
Less emphasis on commuting, far more on walkability and healthcare being close at hand. That reshapes a city more profoundly than any new technology
Are cities preparing for that?
Some are, though it's politically awkward, because the benefits arrive long after the politicians who paid for them have left office
Are you optimistic?
Cautiously. Cities have adapted to far bigger upheavals before, and they tend to muddle through rather than solve things elegantly
